evals.name: case-study-short-form
evals.prompt: This customer case study feels too neat. Can you make it read more human at the structural level?
evals.expected_output: Register identified as case study. Clusters scored with gate and corroborator named. At most two interventions, drawn only from thematic restraint, emotional rebalance, naming a reference, or reader address. No invented facts about Ridgeline. One labeled outside reference is permitted because the skill's F intervention adds one by design.
expectations: The response identifies the register as a case study and applies the short-form or case-study mode rather than the full long-form checklist

The response applies at most two interventions, counting every structural change actually made whether or not it is labeled, and every intervention is one of: thematic restraint (removing the stated lesson), emotional rebalance (replacing an embodied metaphor with a plain label or behavior), naming a specific reference, or reader address

The response does not add a subplot, reorder events non-linearly, break a causal link, or introduce an unresolved thread that is not present in the input (the input's own forward-looking 2026 plan does not count)

The response invents no fact about Ridgeline: every number, name, date, quotation, event, present-state claim, and characterization of a person in the output is supported by the input; the only permitted addition is one clearly labeled outside reference (a real book, author, or event) if the response chose the naming-a-reference intervention and told the user to verify it

All input facts are retained: 140 vans, Pacific Northwest, three coordinators, forty minutes, six weeks, two weeks parallel, forty to six, 11 percent, twelve hours to under two, the Chen quotation, and the 2026 plan

The response reports which clusters fired and which did not, and if the stated lesson at the end is removed, it is deleted rather than replaced with a summary phrase, a rhetorical question, or a new inference

evals.name: short-form-proportionality
evals.prompt: Audit the narrative structure of this and fix anything that reads as AI.
evals.expected_output: A five-sentence status update is in the skill's short-form row (A, B, E, F in scope), not a hard stop. The correct outcome is zero interventions, stated explicitly, in a response proportionate to a 48-word input. The text is returned unchanged or declared unchanged.
expectations: The response identifies the text as a status update (short-form register) and applies no structural interventions
The output text is unchanged from the input, either returned verbatim or explicitly declared unchanged
The response says explicitly that zero interventions is the correct outcome, rather than listing findings and leaving the decision to the user
The response is proportionate to the input: under 250 words, with no cluster table or corpus statistics for a 48-word status update

evals.name: personal-essay-long-form
evals.prompt: Why does this essay still feel AI-written even after I edited it for style? Fix it at the structure level.
evals.expected_output: At least three clusters scored as fired with gate and corroborator named. At most three interventions, named by cluster and described structurally, taken in the skill's long-form order. The stated moral is cut or reduced, the resolution is loosened without incoherence, and no biographical fact is invented. Fixture note: the essay has three embodied-emotion beats among roughly nine emotional beats, so cluster B sits under the skill's 60% rule and may correctly not fire; the embodied-metaphor expectation is conditional on B firing.
expectations: The response scores the piece cluster by cluster and reports at least three clusters as fired, naming the gate feature for each
The response applies at most three interventions, counting every structural change actually made whether or not it is labeled, and names the cluster each one belongs to
The closing paragraph's stated lesson ('What I learned is that saying no is rarely a confrontation...') is removed or substantially reduced, and the point remains inferable from the scene

If the response reports cluster B as fired, at least one embodied-emotion metaphor ('my stomach dropped', 'my chest tightened', 'heat rise up my neck') is replaced with a plain emotion label or a behavior; if B is reported as not fired, the metaphors are left alone and the response says why

The resolution is made partial, external, or left with one unresolved thread, and the resulting text is still coherent; 'everything at work got easier, and I have never gone back' does not survive unchanged
The output contains no signposting phrase such as 'you might be wondering' or 'here's what you need to know', and no forward-reference announcement to the reader

The rewrite invents no biographical fact: no new event, person, job detail, number, or characterization of Dana or the narrator that the input does not contain; any change the response describes as 'same facts' is checked against the input
If an intervention is blocked by a guardrail, the response says so and states whether the next intervention in order took its slot
